goal: parallel-next's in-flight check must never quietly read live sessions as idle, so busy work never looks free to whoever ranks the next work (agent-kit R50).
changed: `inflight.py --sessions` checks every row before it reads anything. A row needs exactly `title`, `cwd`, `running`, `last_active` and `pr_state`, with `running` true or false, `last_active` in ISO 8601 and `pr_state` a string or null.

A row with a `sessionId` is Claude Code desktop's raw `list_sessions` output and is read through `isRunning`, `lastActivityAt` and `prState` (optional, since rows with no pull request leave it out); its other keys are ignored.

A bad row stops the run with exit 1 and no report on stdout. stderr names each bad row, its title, its missing or unknown keys or unreadable values, and the key list. parallel-next steps 1.3 and 1.4 say to pass `list_sessions` output as it is with a high enough `limit`, and never to drop `--sessions` to get past a refusal. bstack 0.62.1.

claims.claim: A hand-written list with isRunning and prState that read a running session's id as free (R99 clear, exit 0) is now refused with exit 1, naming the row, its title, isRunning and prState as unknown and running, last_active and pr_state as missing, and printing nothing on stdout; a row in the raw list_sessions key shape is read as it is and takes R99.
claims.check: inflight.py on the real agent-kit checkout with a --sessions file and an R99 candidate: before on the main checkout at b852f11 (origin/main), after on this branch at e563fab; the raw row uses the key set of a real list_sessions call made this session, with synthetic values. A full real dump (26 rows, limit 200) was also checked: every row has a string title, cwd and lastActivityAt and a boolean isRunning, and a run of the workspace's five-repo command over its rows exited 0
claims.remaining: The real dump is not kept, since it names other projects' sessions. The app may add or drop keys later; only sessionId, title, cwd, isRunning and lastActivityAt are relied on.

claims.claim: A raw list_sessions dump gives the same claims and verdicts as the hand-mapped list of the same sessions (running, recent, old, merged, open and no pull request), rows with unknown keys or unreadable values are refused row by row, and the existing session rules still hold.
claims.check: python3 -m unittest -v tests.test_inflight (20 tests, system Python 3.9, and under Python 3.12); make test (check, validate and the full unit suite) passed on e563fab

claims.claim: The tests hold the rules: seven one-line mutants of the row checks (unknown keys allowed, missing keys allowed, raw rows not recognized, prState required, running not checked, bad last_active accepted, refusal falling through to the report) each turn them red.
claims.check: each mutant of inflight.py followed by python3 -m unittest tests.test_inflight; two survived the first draft of the tests, which were tightened to read each row's own error line
claims.remaining: Seven rules mutated, not every line.

next.source: inferred, from R50's 'Why not done' (that path points at parallel-next's step 1 and never loads the skill)
next.why_now: The script now refuses a bad list and prints the format, so that path can no longer read busy work as free, but a one-line pointer saves the failed first run.
next.impact: A what's-next agent outside the skill passes the dump straight through instead of hand-mapping it and being refused.

next.item: Sessions whose cwd is the workspace folder itself (not a git repo) claim nothing
next.source: inferred, from the full list_sessions run this PR made: running sessions in agent-runtime were dropped because that folder is not one of the repos read
next.why_now: Workspace-level sessions are common (parallel-next and what's-next runs live there); their titles rarely carry an id today, so the gap is small but silent.
next.impact: A session at the workspace root working on an id would claim it in every repo, as one in a workspace repo already does.
